findings.reason: the queue and the DAG order only what the plan declares, so without the edge a §5 node is dispatched before its enabling section lands and its gate cannot pass; with it the node is stored awaiting-upstream and released when the enabling section passes.

findings.reason: as written the clause holds §3 open indefinitely on work no nova node may write, so either the clause moves to a declared cross-repo edge with the landing SHA named as its hand-off, or it is restated as the nova-side obligation (the receipt carries the route) the node can actually prove.
findings.text: §3's third clause requires that "the imas-ambix consumer reads the transport route from the receipt rather than from its own configuration", which is a change in another repository; the plan's own open followup f-20260909T210712175233 (line 110) states plainly that this part "is imas-ambix work against this landing SHA", so no node working in nova can measure or close it

findings.reason: one verdict cannot close three deliverables that land on different evidence (a traced-argument HLO guard, a sweep convergence table, a receipt field set), which is exactly how a section stays open across five runs as this one has.
